Hi @ingo-rauner , thanks for opening these issues, I know that forward secrecy has definitely been discussed here before so I am wondering whether it is part of a different requirement or whether there was a reason for it not being in 11.6. 

Would you be able to check back in the issue history to see if you can find the information? 

See:
https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20%22forward%20secrecy%22

@ingo-rauner, this is addressed by,

| # | Description | Level | #v5.0.be |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **12.1.2** | Verify that only the latest recommended cipher suites are enabled, with the strongest cipher suites set as preferred. L3 applications must only support cipher suites which provide forward secrecy. | 2 | v5.0.be-9.4.1 |

I don't think we would want to include forward secrecy in "V11.6 Public Key Cryptography" because there are legitimate cases of public key cryptography which don't use forward secrecy. For example, non-interactive public-key encryption (as used for Encrypted Client Hello and other usages of HPKE) is typically not forward secret.
